title: Split bookmark
one: Shelf's bookmark cut once down the middle, so its two halves make a pause sign.
idea: Shelf's bookmark cut once down its centre line. The two halves stand as a pause sign, and the round outer shoulders and the two halves of the notch hold them together as one bookmark. A bookmark and a pause both mean stop here and come back later.
built: The shared bookmark (candidates/base: 43.5 dp wide, top at 27.1, shown at 90% about the canvas centre, as every option is: reach 29.29 of 33) with a slot down its centre line 1/7 of its width, 6.21 dp. Each half is 3/7 of the width, 18.64 dp, so the slot is exactly a third of a half; a half is 46.9 dp tall, about 1 : 2.5. I chose the width by eye between 0.12 and 0.15: at 0.12 the slot looked like a crack, and at 0.15 the halves began to come apart in the light colourway. 1/7 is also a ratio the 48 and 32 px cuts can draw exactly (4 px in 28, and 3 in 21 once the 32 px bookmark gains a pixel), so one ratio holds from the launcher down to the 32 px cut; the 16 px cut is 1/9. Each foot runs along the base's notch line to the slot, which meets it 2.01 dp below where the apex was, so the eye carries the V across the slot. Corner rule: a corner's radius follows what made it. The outline makes the square shoulders, which keep 4/34 of the width (5.12 dp); cuts make everything else, the notch's tips and the slot's four corners, and those all take the tips' 1.5/34 (1.92 dp). In the pixel cuts every cut corner is sharp, as the base draws its tips. On the bookmark itself this is the judges' rule by angle (90 degree shoulders at 4/34, 57 degree tips at 1.5/34). It differs only at the slot's two top corners, which are right angles. Drawn at the shoulder radius, each half became a rounded bar and the pair read as II before it read as a bookmark; drawn sharp, they looked harder than the tips at 4× and no different at 1×. At 1× the 1.92 dp corners are 1.3 px, as crisp as the tips beside the 3.4 px shoulders.
corners: A corner's radius follows what made it. The outline makes the square shoulders, which keep 4/34 of the width (5.12 dp); cuts make everything else, the notch's tips and the slot's four corners, and those all take the tips' 1.5/34 (1.92 dp). In the pixel cuts every cut corner is sharp, as the base draws its tips.
small: The 48, 32 and 16 px cuts keep the slot; the glyph is the plain bookmark. 48 px: the base's 28 × 34 px bookmark with a 4 px slot (1/7) between 12 px halves, the feet on the base's notch line (3.3% soft, as the base). 32 px: the base's 20 px bookmark gains a pixel on the left, because a 3 px slot needs an odd width to sit between whole-pixel halves; on 20 px the centred slots nearest 1/7 are 2 px (0.1) and 4 px (0.2, round one's, which read as a pause sign first). So 21 × 24 px with a 3 px slot (1/7), 9 px halves at the base's notch slope, and the mark half a pixel left of the tile's centre (5.7% soft against the base's 5.2: the same 22 soft pixels, a larger share because the slot takes paper away). 16 px: the bookmark gives up its right-hand pixel, 9 × 12 px, so a 1 px slot can sit between two 4 px halves (1/9, the nearest to 1/7 of any bookmark within a pixel of the base's 10 px; round one's 2 px in 10 was 0.2). The feet leave the base's notch line for whole-pixel stairs at 45 degrees, the angle of the brand's own 16 px notch, so they have no soft pixels; they meet the slot 3 px above the tips, level with the base's apex. This mark is also half a pixel left (2.4% soft against the base's 10.9). Glyph: the plain shared bookmark (6.3% soft, as the base). Drawn split, it sat beside the media card's pause button and read as a second pause button, or as 'paused' in the status bar while Shelf was reading aloud; media-card.png in this folder shows both. So the status bar and the media notification show the bookmark, and the split lives in the launcher icon, the launch screens and the browser.
risks: It reads as a pause sign, and pause on its own says something is playing now; it suggests listening only to someone who knows Shelf reads aloud. At 1× on a home screen, in the themed icon and at 16 px it can be taken for a pause button before a bookmark; the round shoulders and sloped feet keep it Shelf's. As the extension's toolbar button, which only saves, it could look like a control that pauses the page; the base's plain bookmark is the safer button there. The notch's apex, the bookmark's most recognisable point, is gone, and the shallow V survives as two sloped feet. The light colourway, ink halves on paper, is the nearest to ElevenLabs' II, the best-known mark in text to speech. Measured from its app icon, ElevenLabs' bars are 1 : 4.8 with square ends, the gap is as wide as a bar (a third of the pair's width), and the pair is 0.63 as wide as it is tall and a quarter of the tile's width. Shelf's halves are 1 : 2.8, the slot is a third of a half (a seventh of the pair), the pair is 0.83 as wide as it is tall and fills 60% of the tile's width, with round outer shoulders and sloped feet. At launcher sizes the difference is plain; at 16 px it comes down to the feet. Also near: a Roman numeral II, a parallel sign, a stock pause button. The mark is two pieces, so any one-colour use (print, emboss, a cut sticker) has to keep the slot open, and at 16 px it is one pixel wide. The 32 and 16 px cuts sit half a pixel left of their tiles' centres: with an odd slot the mark is an odd number of pixels wide, so it can't be centred on an even tile.
